content: Cumulina, a mouse born on December 3, 1997, and deceased on May 5, 2000, was the first animal cloned from adult cells that successfully reached adulthood. She was created using the Honolulu technique, a cloning method developed by the research team led by Ryuzo Yanagimachi, known as Team Yana, at the former campus of the John A. Burns School of Medicine at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa. Cumulina was a brown Mus musculus, commonly referred to as the house mouse. Her name was derived from the cumulus cells, which are the cells surrounding the developing ovarian follicle in mice. In the Honolulu cloning technique, the nuclei from these cumulus cells were transferred into egg cells that had been stripped of their original nuclei. Unlike other mice produced in the Yanagimachi laboratory, which were identified only by numbers, Cumulina was given a name. She was able to produce two healthy litters of offspring and was retired from breeding after the second litter. Cumulina's preserved remains are currently housed at the Institute for Biogenesis Research laboratory in Honolulu, Hawaii, which is part of the John A. Burns School of Medicine. Some of her descendants have been displayed at the Bishop Museum in Honolulu and the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago, Illinois.
